notes.real_loadouts: named loadouts a real Sufa was seen carrying, offered on the Loadout screen beside the mission's (front-end.md §10.1, badge Operational). Air-to-air, long range: the IAF's picture of Sufa 816 in its shelter (twz-sufa-816): an AIM-120 on the left wingtip, 1, a Python 5 on each mid pylon, 3 / 7, a large tank on each inboard pylon, 4 / 6 (600 US gal inferred from their size), a tank on the centreline, 11 (the real 5; the 300 US gal inferred: our only centreline tank), no chin pods. The right wing's outer part is out of the picture: 9's AIM-120 inferred as 1's mirror, 8 left empty (inferred); the left outboard rail, 2, is hidden behind the tank and the wingtip missile, left empty (inferred). The missiles told by their shapes (inferred: the AIM-120's mid-body wings, the Python 5's canards). No sourced strike or SEAD loadout of our stores was found: the IAF's strike pictures show four Rampage missiles (not a store of ours) or a pair of GBU-31s with the other stations out of view (modern-iaf/docs/data-formats.md, the loadouts' open list)
notes.positions: each station's place on the wing as the Loadout screen names it: 1 / 9 the wingtip rails, 2 / 8 outboard, 3 / 7 mid, 4 / 6 inboard (the wet stations), 5 the targeting pod's chin hardpoint under the right intake (the real jet's 5R; inferred from the F-16's station numbering), 10 the navigation pod's chin hardpoint under the left intake (the real jet's 5L, numbered after the wing's nine: the engine's pylon J), 11 the centreline under the fuselage (the real jet's 5, numbered after 5L: the engine's pylon K)
notes.labels: the real names of the chin hardpoints, 5R (the sim's 5) and 5L (the sim's 10), and of the centreline, 5 (the sim's 11; f16net-300: the F-16's 300 gal tank on the centerline), shown in place of their numbers: the F-16's navigation pod on 5L (f16net-lantirn), the targeting pod on the other (inferred, modern-iaf/docs/research/pods.md §2.3)
notes.lateral_limit_kgm: the F-16's maximum allowable asymmetric (rolling) moment, 25,020 ft-lb (3,459 kg·m), as a forum quotes the flight manual's stores limitations (bms-asym; the manual itself not seen, so inferred); the Sufa's and the Barak's taken the same (inferred)
notes.lateral_limit_hard: false: the briefing warns and lets the jet fly (the manual forbids the take-off only when the roll trim cannot hold the moment, which the briefing does not know)
notes.allowed: the stores each station takes, by its real number. Sourced: the AIM-9 and the AIM-120 on 1 / 9, 2 / 8 and 3 / 7 (f16net-aim9, f16net-aim120); the GBU-31 on 3 / 7, one each, and the GBU-38 there two to a BRU-57/A (120.2 kg, l3h-bru57; f16net-jdam); three Mk 82 on a TER-9/A (47.6 kg, ter-9a) on 3 / 7, and on 4 / 6 (f16net-mk82, a forum: inferred; with tanks on 4 / 6 the real jet takes two on 3 / 7, not modelled); the 370 US gal tank on 4 / 6 (f16net-tanks) and the 600 US gal tank there (usaf-600); the 300 US gal tank on the centreline, 11 (the real 5), with the 600s and the chin pods (commons-857: a Sufa with two 600 gal tanks and a centreline tank). The Python 5 on 3 / 7 (twz-sufa-816: the IAF's picture of Sufa 816 shows one on each mid pylon; the missile told by its canards and four rear fins, inferred). Inferred: the Python 5 on the AIM-9 rails 1 / 9 and 2 / 8 (a modified LAU-129; no station chart found); the Mk 83 and the Mk 84 one each on 3 / 7 and 4 / 6 (f16net-mk82 tells of four Mk 84); the SPICE 1000 / 2000 on 3 / 7 and 4 / 6 (no source gives their stations); the Delilah on none (dropped 2026-11-14: no cruise-missile flight class); the Sufa and the Barak the same (no source shows a difference) but for the Python 5 on 3 / 7, seen on the Sufa only. Each rack's rack_drag (drag index, flight-model.md §9.18) inferred as one of its stores' (a beam of about their cross-section). The laser-guided GBU-12, GBU-16 and GBU-10 (sufa-at) one each on 3 / 7 and 4 / 6, as the Mk 82 to Mk 84 bodies they are built on (inferred); the targeting pod (the Litening, sufa-at) on the right chin hardpoint (twz-litening: a chin station; the right side inferred from photos), the sim's station 5 (the user's yes to the pod and the laser bombs on the F-16s, 17 Nov 2026, avionics-plan.md §8.2); the LANTIRN navigation pod, AN/AAQ-13, on the left chin hardpoint, 10 (5L): the IAF names the two pods under the Sufa's intake (iaf-f16i), the F-16 carries the navigation pod on 5L (f16net-lantirn); carried, drawn and weighed only, its functions later (modern-iaf/docs/research/pods.md P7, P8)
notes.tail: the number the game draws on the player's Sufa (shared/extra/models/f16/f16i.tail.json `number`, docs/aircraft-models.md §1.6: F-16I 846 of 201 Squadron, whose paint the model wears, also at Ramon; docs/f16i.md §8.1; every other jet shows its own), so every screen shows the jet the player sees (the user, 2026-11-13, A31). Until then 482 of 253 Squadron (jp-482); the squadron since then the model's, 201 (the base file's `squadrons`; the user, 2026-11-13)
notes.max_takeoff_kg: the F-16I's maximum take-off weight, 23,582 kg (about 52,000 lb), which its F100-PW-229 IPE allows
notes.type: the F-16's type code, the one the shared code keys the F-16 family on; the airframe definition f16i makes it the Sufa
notes.model: none: the player's jet is drawn from its airframe definition (shared/extra/planes/f16i/airframe.json)
notes.scale: 1: our models are built true size
notes.radius_m: half the span over the wingtip rails, 9.96 m
notes.strength: our damage scale's fighter (modern-iaf/docs/data-formats.md, damage scale)
notes.loadout.20mm: M61A1, 511 rounds (the F-16's; the two-seat Sufa's count is not published, inferred the same)
notes.loadout.chaff: no public count found; 60 held until one is
notes.loadout.flare: no public count found; 60 held until one is
notes.pylons: an AIM-9M on each wingtip rail (stations 1 and 9, A and I): the F-16's wingtip rails carry its short-range missiles; the Sufa's two wingtip missiles are standard (mf-f16i), its usual one the Python 5 (aft-f16i), which the sim has no record of yet, so the AIM-9M stands in (inferred); a 370 US gal tank on each wing's inboard station (stations 4 and 6, D and F; the Sufa's options list two 370 gal wing tanks, ipms-f16i), carried on most flights (inferred); no other underwing stores in training (inferred); an AIM-9M on each underwing missile station, 2 / 8 (B, H) and 3 / 7 (C, G): the F-16 carries AIM-9s and AIM-120s there (f16net-aim9, f16net-aim120); on 2 / 8 the AIM-9M stands in for the IAF's Python (aft-f16i on the Sufa, inferred on the Barak), on 3 / 7 for an AIM-120, which the sim has no record of yet (stand-ins, inferred)
notes.inventory: the stores the briefing lists as the jet's, each its own record in data/db/weapons with its sourced weight and size: the AIM-9M, the Python 5, the AIM-120, the Mk 82, Mk 83 and Mk 84, the GBU-31 and GBU-38 JDAM, the SPICE 1000 and 2000, the 370 and 600 US gal tanks and the 300 US gal centreline tank; no counts published
